column1: # A/B workloads for dev/perf/ab.sh (see dev/profiling/PLAN.md §3-§4).
# Format:  <name> <sets> <program arguments...>
#   sets      comma-separated set names; the first set listed decides the verdict metric:
#             cpu -> cycles:u (deterministic --cpu 0 runs), reader -> user+kernel cycles, else wall time
#   D/        the benchmark data dir (~/.cache/hmmer-bench/derived-*, see dev/bench)
#   F/        ab fixtures dir (made on demand by the @fixture lines below)
#   $NCPU     number of online CPUs
# Each run executes in its own empty dir; every file it writes, plus stdout and stderr,
# is compared between A and B after the dev/bench normalization (dates, timings).
# Threaded runs with E-value thresholds set -Z to the true number of targets. Without -Z,
# each worker uses its own running sequence count as Z (src/p7_pipeline.c:580), so which
# unreported borderline hits stay in the hit list depends on thread scheduling. The longest
# kept name sets column widths in the main output and --tblout (src/p7_tophits.c:1134),
# making those widths flaky upstream. Reported hits/E-values equal the -Z-less run's.
# Serial (--cpu 0) runs are deterministic and keep the default Z. X1_..._defZ keeps the
# default (no -Z) on purpose: ab.sh accepts whitespace-only (column padding) differences.
# Fixtures: @fixture <file it creates> <shell command>, run in F/ with the A snapshot's
# programs first on PATH, only when <file> is missing.
@fixture Pfam-A.hmm.h3m  ln -sf D/Pfam-A.hmm Pfam-A.hmm && hmmpress Pfam-A.hmm > /dev/null
# ---- cpu: single-threaded, deterministic; judge by cycles:u (instructions:u shown too)
W1_hitters_10k      cpu        --cpu 0 -o main.out -A ali.sto --tblout t.tbl --domtblout t.dom D/pfam_hitters.hmm D/sprot_10k.fa
W2_mix_10k          cpu        --cpu 0 -o main.out --tblout t.tbl --domtblout t.dom D/pfam_len_mix.hmm D/sprot_10k.fa
W3_m200_sprot       cpu        --cpu 0 --noali -o main.out --tblout t.tbl --domtblout t.dom D/kern_M200.hmm D/sprot.fa
W4_med_longseqs     cpu        --cpu 0 -o main.out --domtblout t.dom D/pfam_len_med.hmm D/sprot_long.fa
W5_med_1k_max       cpu        --cpu 0 --max -o main.out --domtblout t.dom D/pfam_len_med.hmm D/sprot_1k.fa
# ---- reader: the FASTA parser's share of CPU is large (~55%: a short model, all of Swiss-Prot);
# single-threaded, judge by user + kernel cycles: they include reading the file (system calls,
# page-cache copies) and, unlike task-clock, don't move with the CPU clock rate
R1_m50_sprot        reader     --cpu 0 --noali -o main.out --tblout t.tbl D/kern_M50.hmm D/sprot.fa
# ---- scale: reader-bound thread scaling; judge by interleaved wall time
X1_p100_50k_c4      scale      --cpu 4 -Z 51857 --noali -o main.out --tblout t.tbl D/pfam_100.hmm D/sprot_50k.fa
X1_p100_50k_c8      scale      --cpu 8 -Z 51857 --noali -o main.out --tblout t.tbl D/pfam_100.hmm D/sprot_50k.fa
X1_p100_50k_cN      scale      --cpu $NCPU -Z 51857 --noali -o main.out --tblout t.tbl D/pfam_100.hmm D/sprot_50k.fa
X1_p100_50k_cN_defZ scale      --cpu $NCPU --noali -o main.out --tblout t.tbl D/pfam_100.hmm D/sprot_50k.fa
X2_m200_sprot_cN    scale      --cpu $NCPU -Z 570420 --noali -o main.out --tblout t.tbl --domtblout t.dom D/kern_M200.hmm D/sprot.fa
# ---- query: per-query fixed costs (many models x small DB)
X3_p1k_s1k_c0       query      --cpu 0 -o main.out --tblout t.tbl D/pfam_1k.hmm D/sprot_1k.fa
X3_p1k_s1k_cN       query      --cpu $NCPU -Z 999 -o main.out --tblout t.tbl D/pfam_1k.hmm D/sprot_1k.fa
X4_pfamA_txt_c0     query      --cpu 0 -o main.out --tblout t.tbl D/Pfam-A.hmm D/q_pick5.fa
X4_pfamA_txt_cN     query      --cpu $NCPU -Z 5 -o main.out --tblout t.tbl D/Pfam-A.hmm D/q_pick5.fa
X4_pfamA_h3m_c0     query      --cpu 0 -o main.out --tblout t.tbl F/Pfam-A.hmm.h3m D/q_pick5.fa
X4_pfamA_h3m_cN     query      --cpu $NCPU -Z 5 -o main.out --tblout t.tbl F/Pfam-A.hmm.h3m D/q_pick5.fa
# many queries x a small db, as --dbcache is meant for (both A and B need the option)
X3_p1k_s1k_cN_dbc   query      --cpu $NCPU --dbcache -Z 999 -o main.out --tblout t.tbl D/pfam_1k.hmm D/sprot_1k.fa
X4_pfamA_h3m_cN_dbc query      --cpu $NCPU --dbcache -Z 5 -o main.out --tblout t.tbl F/Pfam-A.hmm.h3m D/q_pick5.fa
# ---- milestone: realistic annotation run (~1 min per run today); --cut_ga thresholds are
# bit scores, so no -Z is needed for determinism
X5_human_pfam1k_cN  milestone  --cpu $NCPU --cut_ga --tblout t.tbl --domtblout t.dom -o /dev/null D/pfam_1k.hmm D/human.fa
X5_human_pfam1k_cN_dbc milestone --cpu $NCPU --dbcache --cut_ga --tblout t.tbl --domtblout t.dom -o /dev/null D/pfam_1k.hmm D/human.fa
